text: I'm afraid, my friends, the Daleks have won.
What guarantee is there that you won't fire your guns afterwards, hmm?
There is no guarantee that the object he is carrying...
Surrender it!
He will not...
Silence! You will not speak!
You dare not fire because of this terranium.
To end this stalemate, may I suggest...
There will be no more discussion.
Discussion? The core is to be handed over.
Prepare to exterminate them, creatures.
How do I keep going?
Stay dead. Search for the fugitives.
There's only one guard.
Now, you know what to do?
Yes.
It'll never work.
It will. It's got to.
The other Daleks will be back here before he can get started.
Why should they?
They're not looking for us. They won't expect us to come back here.
Look, they're not complete fools.
They know we've got to get off Myra and that their ship is our only chance.
Don't worry.
Like most of the Doctor's plans, this one's simple. It won't take long.
Well, why doesn't he get started, then?
Give him time. He's got to get round there.
Look, you must learn to trust him.
He's had dealings with the Daleks before.
I have no choice.
Let's hope you're right.
He should be in position by now.
Come on.
I've come to give myself up.
Do you have the terranium?
I have.
I realize, of course, that I am no match.
For the Daleks.
So, if I hand it over, will you help me and my friends to get away from this planet?
Where are the others?
Oh, they will come when I call them.
The terranium.
Shall I give it to you, or would you prefer me to hand it to you in your ship?
You will wait there until the patrol returns.
The others are to join you.
My tin friend, never.
You mustn't forget that I came here and surrendered.
I have surrendered to my own free will.
Help! Help!
Loss of vision! Loss of vision!
I'm under attack! I'm under attack!
Patrol alert! Patrol alert!
Spiring before we sustain damage!
Report the fugitives boarded the pursuit ship!
I'm quite accustomed to this Dalek technique.
Close the hatches.
Doors are not closing.
That's your lock reading. 2.24.
Oh, the power buildup is far too slow. Feed in that extra energy.
3.82. Rising.
That ship activated. 5-0-0.
Pull me up to attack.
4.32. Still rising.
Splendid.
Prepare to board the ship. Exterminate them!
Too close.
Portal gyro. Gyro down, Mo.
Coding 9-2. Red.
Red.
Blue. Blue.
Discharge.
Coding 1-0-0.
All blue reading. Take off.
Ready. Now.
Hold tight.
Is this my greeting?
I agree that my mission was to return to Earth and recover the Terranium.
This I have not done.
Failure will not be tolerated.
But I did notify you of the fugitives' whereabouts.
The planet Mira.
There, the vital core can be taken from them without suspicion.
Their presence on Earth was a constant danger.
At any time, they could have contacted forces unsympathetic to our plans.
You make your incompetence sound like an achievement.
Incompetence now, is it?
You forget that the original blunder was not of my doing.
I journeyed to and from Earth to correct a failing your security force
should have dealt with.
The core was stolen from here.
My actions have brought about a situation
which will allow you to recover the missing Terranium easily and simply.
If that is a failure, then I have failed.
You had the audacity to accuse me, Mavic Chen, of incompetence.
A Dalek pursuit ship stolen?
It is not.
Really?
It is not an emergency.
No.
No.
More like a catastrophe.
They may believe that they have successfully escaped from us.
Good work, Doctor.
No, of course it won't, my dear boy, that's the whole point.
I mean your plan.
No, we shall have to make a copy.
A copy so exact that we can deceive the Daleks.
They'll still want this Terranium back, you know.
They won't rest until they get it.
Yes, but suppose...
There isn't time to suppose.
I'm sure the Doctor can copy it well enough.
Yes, thank you, thank you, my dear, thank you.
I'll have a good try,
and I think that will give us sufficient breathing space.
What's that?
We're changing course.
We're moving away on a selected route.
Good gracious, we're out of course for the Panic Kemble.
You know, I'm very much afraid that we are under the Dalek influence.
It's obviously this that's causing the damage.
That settles that.
Well, isn't that rather a drastic way of dealing with things?
Oh, Sarah, the technology of my age
may be hundreds of years well in yours and the Doctor's,
but there are still some things I can handle.
Yes, of course it is, my dear boy.
Of course there is.
Come along, young lady.
Let's get on with our mineral whilst we still have the time.
I sincerely hope there's not been any further bungling.
We have carefully lost control,
but once the magnetized beam reaches them...
After we have the core of the Time Destructor in our possession,
I trust...
Of course! Of course!
You think so?
Yes, yes.
There, that's a good copy.
Or do I say it myself?
Yes, but there's still a problem of charging it.
The Daleks will know immediately that it isn't the real Terranium.
I appreciate that, young lady,
but this is the right balance and the right weight.
We're still on our own course.
The Daleks haven't attempted to divert us yet.
Oh, good, good, good. Well, you keep watching.
That's a good fellow.
Hey!
No, I should try that one.
This is excellent.
Isn't it?
How do you propose to activate it?
Oh, we're working on that. Yes, we're working on it.
We could use the Gravity Force from the ship's power center.
Well, I mean, there's an outlet here.
What?
What's wrong with that?
Too primitive, my boy.
Too primitive and far too dangerous.
Gravity Force as a source of energy was abandoned centuries ago.
We were still using it.
Oh, yes, and the Romans used treadmills.
I still think G-Force would do the trick.
We're changing course again.
Back to the planet Kemble?
You know, it appears that we're affected by magnetization.
We're being held in a very strong beam.
That will take us right back to the Daleks.
Well, let's try and break it down.
Come along.
I want to see about those treadmills.
Stephen.
My dear boy.
What? What's happened?
He's still breathing.
The fool.
He's still breathing.
He's tried his experiment with G-Force and Reliance Power.
Oh.
He's still alive.
He's lucky at that.
But it's worked.
Look, Doctor.
It's just like the real terranium.
Oh, isn't that wonderful?
That's wonderful.
Stephen's theory has proved successful.
But what about the poor boy?
It appears that you have at last succeeded in getting the terranium back.
Of course.
And we shall deal with these fugitives
as with all...
No.
Of course not.
But might it not be advisable for me to return them to Earth for trial?
Why?
They will be tried and found guilty as traitors to the solar system.
After all, the woman is from Earth.
The Daleks will deal with them.
There is no need for the delay in their extermination.
Some people on Earth know that our traitors were transparent.
They will be exposed tomorrow.
If they disappear for good,
those people will be curious and ask what happened to them.
It's possible that they might find out that the Daleks executed them.
Then your plans could be hindered.
It is essential that you do not allow your Earth people...
Human curiosity is something I can have no control over.
You must forestall their questions.
Too late.
Yes.
It is possible.
Once we have the terranium...
Very well.
I leave their fate to you.
The Dalek reception force should now be in position at the specified landing point.
Yes, they should.
And I think it's about time we left to join them.
Don't you?
Height and speed reducing.
Yes, we should be landing in about five minutes.
I'll see how Stephen is.
I think the effect's wearing off.
No, my dear, he's adapting to it.
Can you talk, my boy?
No, he's still under the influence of that force field.
Nothing further will happen to you.
Now, don't worry.
Yes, nothing further is going to happen to him,
but I must confess I have no cure for that condition.
He's enclosed in a force field.
Yes, yes, I'm afraid so.
Sarah, will you bring me that fake terranium, hmm?
Hmm.
Yes, yes, yes.
Now, listen to me, Stephen.
Try and understand.
This is very important, so you must trust me.
You do understand.
Just try and indicate.
Now we've got to face the Daleks.
Open the doors, please.
Stephen will lead the way.
This way, Stephen.
But it won't.
It won't work.
It's our only chance, my dear.
And remember, I will do all the talking, hmm?
The terranium.
I would suggest that you give that to me, young man.
No.
And remember, you cannot fire because of the terranium.
You have another 50 years' work, hmm?
Possibly, but you are still in no position to bargain.
I will hand over the terranium outside my ship, the TARDIS.
You heard the condition.
It is not acceptable.
You heard what the Dalek Supreme said.
Outside my ship, the TARDIS.
Oh, no, where?
He seems determined.
Does it really matter?
Very well.
In front of his ship.
Thank you.
Stephen, kingdom.
Traitor.
Sarah, open the door, please.
The young man will give you the terranium
when the girl and I are safely inside my ship, the TARDIS.
Very well.
Making sure of your escape, eh, Doctor?
Remember to do exactly as I say, Stephen.
I will give you further instructions from inside my TARDIS.
Inside the TARDIS.
I'm destructed.
The Dalek guns must have destroyed that force field completely.
It's a good thing they didn't fire a second time.
I don't really know what happened.
You were enclosed in a field of gravity force and reliance power.
You had a shield around, you know, similar to that one that protects the TARDIS.
Oh, that reminds me.
Where is that genuine terranium, hmm?
Over here.
It's a pity I've blacked out.
I mean, if I knew the ratio readings,
we could use the same force again to protect us from the Daleks.
Certainly not.
What you did was very dangerous and extremely stupid.
Come off it, it worked.
One more experiment like that and you really will be dead.
Nonsense.
Now, now, now, you listen to me, young man.
I warned you it was dangerous before you tried it.
You might have killed yourself and blown up the spaceship.
Then where would we all be, hmm?
I know where I'd be. I don't know about you.
Now, now, now, don't be cheeky.
Look, if it hadn't been for me,
how would you have charged the terranium and carried out the handover?
I think we should experiment further.
I don't care what you think.
We're not going to repeat it.
Why do you think science turned down your discovery, hmm?
Because it isn't safe.
So perhaps in future, you'll pay attention to what I say.
And remember that I happen to be the leader of this expedition.
And I don't want to keep on repeating myself.
But Doctor, it's...
If you don't like it, you can get off, hmm?
Hmm?
All right, Doctor, I promise I won't experiment with it any further.
I hope not.
Something's gone wrong.
What's the matter, hmm?
It's stopped going up and down.
Well, that means we've landed.
Oh, that scanner's not working, hmm?
Can you mend it?
Yes, I shall have to repair it, of course, yes, yes.
But that means check it up with the whole circuit.
Let's get on with it.
Don't you dare touch that.
Why not?
But just look at those dials, look.
Look here, Sarah.
You see those dials?
Now, do you know what that means?
If either of you went outside, it would be extremely dangerous.
The whole atmosphere is entirely poisonous.
